reason: Follow-up to Stream K: operator-help retrieval gains a relevance floor. search_operator_help keeps the best match and only those that hold up against it (an article whose keyword phrase the question contains as whole words needs a third of the best score; a match on shared vocabulary alone needs three quarters), and chat's _retrieve_operator_help asks for at most three articles (was eight). Scoring and ranking are unchanged. Engagement-knowledge retrieval is deliberately unchanged (measured: no embedding floor separates relevant from irrelevant chunks). Selected: operator-help ranking tests (new cases), test_chat.py (help citations, knowledge, synthesis wiring), the Stream K reference-material tests (tightened citation list), the tool loop (final-synthesis help path), and knowledge retrieval/timing tests that run prepare with retrieval. Counts from pytest --collect-only.
exclusions: No frontend, native or Playwright tests: no UI or visible change; citations render as before, only fewer weakly related help articles are sent and cited. test_packaging.py excluded: the bundled operator_help.md corpus is unchanged. No full suite.
